title: Orchestration Patterns: Supervisor, Swarm, Hierarchical
service: Orchestra: supervisors that route through a routing LLM, a JSON topology snapshot, a context-budget hierarchy planner, tool-call supervision over JSON-RPC 2.0, and deterministic keyword routing with backtracking and a trace of every pick
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no network and no LLM: the routing LLM and the specialists are deterministic objects the tests supply
deviations: Part 1 leaves the swarm out: the plan's swarm defect (hops run out and the task is dropped) is the hop-counter trap of lesson 16, which this lesson is told to avoid. Part 1 instead debugs the supervisor itself: prompt folding, the nested outcome, the lesson code's default-to-sales fallback, and the prompt rebuilt on every decision.

Part 1 has no separate top/sub classify mismatch: with members owned per supervisor the hierarchy is consistent by construction. Its hierarchical defect is the nested outcome instead (a supervisor passes its sub-supervisor's outcome through without its own hop, so the hierarchy looks as cheap as one level), and the fallback to the first member is the defect that sends tasks to the wrong specialist. Lesson 12's Part 1 plants the raw-label lookup in route(), so this route() already strips the router's reply.

Part 2 models the router field as model name / null / missing, mapping the lesson's Crew (LLM router) and Flow (deterministic) modes plus inheritance; tuples for members and keywords give the round-trip type trap.
Part 3 returns a Topology from Part 2 and adds team keywords (members' keywords without repeats), which Part 5's routing uses.

Part 5 ships tokenize() in the starter: substring matching and word splitting are already main traps of lesson 26 (Part 1) and lesson 08 (Part 3), so here the 'debugger' and 'Quote,' tasks are side checks. Its main traps are the backtracking rule and the Build It trace (one line per pick, empty picks and backtracks included, indented like code/main.py's hierarchical trace). The backtrack cap stays a cap on search, not a hop counter: hop counting is lesson 16's Part 1 defect, and a team reached again on its own path raises ValueError, so picks cannot bounce.

parts.lesson_anchor: Supervisor-worker (central router; specialists do not talk to each other); Hierarchical; Build It (per-pattern trace and op count, hierarchical is deepest); code/main.py classify (unknown intents fall back to sales) and hierarchical (one op and one trace line per level)
planted_bugs: prompt() only strips descriptions, so a multi-line description spills onto a second line; the failure surfaces inside the test's routing LLM stub ('prompt line is not a member'), one call away from prompt()

run() hands a sub-supervisor's outcome back as it is (return member.run(task)), so the path starts below the supervisor that got the task and the op count leaves out its own routing decision: desk -> customer_ops -> bug reports 2 ops instead of 3
a reply that names no member falls back to the first member, like main.py's return "sales", instead of ESCALATE; a reply that names another team's worker (refund, asked of commercial) escalates too
prompt() rebuilds every member line on every routing decision: 800 tasks over 3000 workers
parts.timing_assert: 800 routing decisions over 3000 workers under 0.04 s. Measured on this machine (Python 3.12.14, other agents running, load average 4-9): rebuilt prompt 0.45-1.1 s, cached prompt 0.51-1.33 ms. Registering 3000 workers under 0.05 s: 0.15-0.38 ms as shipped and in the reference, 0.74-1.34 s when register rebuilds the prompt eagerly, 5.5-7 ms when register appends one line to a cached prompt string
parts.overfix_guard: a worker registered between two batches gets its tasks and appears in the prompt (rules out a cache that never invalidates); registering stays cheap (rules out rebuilding in register, O(N^2)); the exact prompt text rules out deleting newlines, or replacing each one with a space, instead of folding whitespace; a reply naming another team's worker escalates (rules out escalating on the literal reply none only)
